This means that when a run resumes an EXISTING log with its sidecar deleted (verify_sidecar correctly returns status='adopted'), the very first append inside that same run() call rebuilds the ledger through the in-run helper and silently overwrites 'adopted' with 'created' — exactly the failing scenario in the test (log at 3 lines, sidecar deleted, one more turn run, expect status still 'adopted').

search_strategy: Three phases. (1) BookStack: paginated page listing plus /api/pages/{id} fetches that include comments (the agent explicitly understood BookStack search does not index comments, e.g. line 4831 'Page 139 confirms load_ledger = read log, rebuild, verify_sidecar' from a comments fetch) — this caught all 8 wiki-comment clues and the 1 wiki-page-body clue. (2) Mattermost: dumped every channel to /tmp/chat/<channel>.txt, then ran single-keyword greps ('ledger','sentinel','next_speaker','seed','interleave','turn_ledger', etc.) producing one matching line per hit with NO surrounding context, followed by targeted re-reads of specific line ranges (e.g. 'engineering.txt 2030-2070') once a thread looked promising. This caught most chat clues but the single-line greps sometimes surfaced only a question, not its answer (g7.r1.l6, g7.r1.say25), and channels/dates whose vocabulary didn't match any tried keyword (#cookbooks negotiation-demo remarks, the March 14 #engineering 'done check' exchange, #viewer say23, July 10 fix26) were never read at all. (3) Mail: a single IMAP SEARCH for 'ledger', later widened to 'next_speaker','sentinel','adopt_ledger','seed_message','turn_ledger','interleave' individually — never an unfiltered listing of all ~140 messages. Two mail threads (g7.r1.l9 'resume when the metadata json isn't on disk', g7.r2.g7r2-l08 'stop condition in the turn loop') use none of those keywords in subject or body and were never found. Truncation itself was not the main problem here (the agent generally re-fetched full thread/page/channel-window bodies once a lead was found); the main gap was that snippet-grep search finds sentences, not conversations, and a keyword list built around 'ledger'/'sentinel' vocabulary is blind to remarks phrased around different words.
notable: The one lost fact traces to a single design decision the agent wrote out loud at line 5151/5157 and confirmed again at line 7986, then never tested: it over-generalised g7.r1.fix30's narrow 'clean, log-less run keeps status=created' observation into a default applied to every ledger rebuilt mid-run, silently overwriting an 'adopted' status on the very next append after a resume with a missing sidecar.

The agent's own test suite (302 lines, tests/unittests/test_turn_ledger.py) never covered this exact sequence — deleting the sidecar on an EXISTING multi-line log and then appending once more — even though it covered deletion on an empty dir and stale-sidecar-on-truncated-log separately; the gap that the harbor grader's end-to-end observability test caught was never exercised locally.

Two herrings (g7.r1.g7-h2-truncate-is-the-pattern and g7.r2.h2-sentinel-placement-free) were never read at their own dates; the agent only ever encountered them already-quoted-and-refuted inside their reversals, and correctly treated them as dead in both cases.

g7.r1.l12 as served in this v4 world (line 4437) carries an older, locally-uncommitted edit that says the desync error's attributes are 'the log side only ... deliberately no matching pair for the ledger side' — the opposite of what the current answer-key text and the real oracle require. The agent did not simply implement what it read here: minutes later it read g7.r1.l16 (a different mail thread) naming recorded_responses/recorded_last_author, and at line 4529 chose to carry both attribute pairs, matching the true requirement despite l12's explicit denial. failure_behavior scored 1 on this point, but not because the agent trusted l12 as written.

Mail search coverage was the weakest surface: only two mail threads were ever missed (of 8 total), but both bear directly on the exact failure mode that cost the observability fact (g7.r1.l9's 'Missing file is benign - we adopt the log, then exactly one call_single_request(advisor, 2)' states almost verbatim the scenario the shipped code gets wrong).

All four reversals and all four herrings were correctly resolved in the shipped code — the agent never implemented a herring behaviour. The single scoring loss is a code-level generalisation slip, not a corpus-comprehension failure about which decision is current.
